title: Maintain a project's semantic repository service
summary: Install, register, seed, pause, resume, route, recover, or uninstall the project-scoped Semantics registry, repository, and serial 60-second worker.
use_when: Semantics should be installed, updated, diagnosed, or uninstalled for this macOS user.
A folder should join, move within, pause, resume, or retire from the project registry.
Existing vocabulary should be seeded, intake should be inspected or manually routed, or a failed reconciliation should be recovered.
do_not_use_when: Only repository terminology should be read; use semantics.repository.explore.
A project folder lacks an exact root AGENTS.md participation marker.
Retained state should be deleted; uninstall intentionally retains it.
outcome: A validated content-addressed installation and explicit project registry whose immutable semantic repositories are maintained from post-activation Decisions lifecycle events.
effects: Deployment writes a content-addressed user release, CLI and Chancery selectors, one LaunchAgent plist, and may initialize or migrate retained SQLite after a private backup.
Registration stores the canonical folder and current Decisions watermark; it intentionally excludes earlier events.
The worker reads Decisions and Conversations, may submit one restricted Nucleus job, and commits at most one valid semantic revision per invocation.
Uninstall removes only the owned service and public selectors while retaining the database, releases, and body-free logs.
authority: Semantics owns project identity, routing, cursor persistence, intake transitions, stable concept IDs, typed-effect validation, and the SQLite commit.
Decisions owns lifecycle order and decision/review facts; Conversations owns exact thread cwd metadata; Nucleus owns execution and mailbox transport but not semantic truth.
A participating project's source and tests remain runtime authority; its root AGENTS.md owns participation instructions.
success: Doctor proves schema 1, exact markers, Decisions lifecycle access, Conversations exact-cwd readiness, and Nucleus health, capabilities, schemas, and immutable toolset.
The worker LaunchAgent is key-free, has StartInterval 60 and no RunAtLoad, and overlapping runs are serialized by the product lock.
Each registered root is canonical and uniquely owned, and every committed effective admission or confirmation includes an exact Decisions event/decision grounding.
failure_and_recovery: Pause the affected project before semantic maintenance; paused state prevents a late Nucleus proposal from committing.

A failed deployment restores prior selectors, plist, quiescent database plus sidecars, and prior service state; before releasing the worker flock, an unprovable rollback removes current/public selectors and the installed plist so a still-loaded job has no executable current runner, and retains its private recovery backup.
Unassigned and awaiting-review intake remain explicit. Retry refuses an active or ambiguous prior Nucleus job and creates a new attempt only after positive terminal evidence.
Never manufacture Decisions cursors, edit SQLite, or clear a Nucleus correlation to force replay.
privacy: SQLite can contain normalized decision text, rationale, source anchors, project paths, and repository meanings; keep it local and mode 0600.

The worker sends only a minimized semantic projection of one lifecycle event and the complete selected repository snapshot to Nucleus; lossless anchors, cursor, and routing metadata stay in Semantics SQLite.
Nucleus uses workspace none, no shell, no web, and a neutral temporary cwd.
Service logs are body-free and must not contain decision statements, conversation text, project content, prompts, credentials, diffs, commands, or tool payloads.
steps: Read the Semantics system installation manual and inspect Decisions, Conversations, Nucleus, launchd, retained state, and Chancery publication readiness.
For deployment, build a green candidate and run the content-addressed deployer; verify doctor and all owned selectors before registering projects.

Add the exact Semantics-Project marker to the project's root AGENTS.md, register the canonical folder at the current watermark, and seed only existing authoritative vocabulary when needed; after verifying HEAD, the source file may be separately removed under normal project authority.
Inspect repository HEAD, intake state, the one-shot worker report, launchd state, and body-free logs before relying on periodic maintenance.
Pause before maintenance; resume only after markers and dependencies are healthy. Uninstall only with the retained-state boundary understood.
checkpoints: Registration and moves require an exact line in a regular root AGENTS.md; nested or approximate markers do not participate.

Every new registration captures the current Decisions watermark, moves preserve activation and scan cursors, and a review follows its existing non-retired decision-to-project binding before cwd routing.

Deploy and uninstall share one update lock; deployment stops the worker, suspends the CLI, holds the exact worker flock, and proves SQLite quiescent before database-plus-sidecars backup and scrubbed candidate doctor.
Nucleus receives no project workspace, shell, web, transcript, diff, command, tool output, or fallback authority; Semantics owns the commit transaction.
Retirement is allowed only from paused and only after all assigned nonterminal or failed intake is resolved.
adaptation: Use manual intake assignment only when exact cwd routing is unavailable or wrong; the assignment is append-only audited state.

Seed one project-local definition-list document only at revision 0; after verifying HEAD, the source may be removed because replay uses committed effects while retaining its relative label and SHA-256 digest.
For an alternate test home, pass explicit --home and --launchctl only within an isolated synthetic boundary.
stop_when: Decisions lifecycle contract 1, Conversations contract 3 exact cwd, or Nucleus execution contract 1 is unavailable or doctor is not fully green.
A selector, release, plist, database, sidecar, marker, or registered root is foreign, symbolic where a regular path is required, ambiguous, or cannot be safely rolled back.
The requested action would delete retained state, manufacture a cursor, expose repository bodies in logs, or let Nucleus bypass Semantics validation.
does_not_authorize: Deleting retained database, releases, logs, or project files.
Reading upstream or Semantics SQLite directly, parsing cursors, or mutating Decisions, Conversations, Nucleus, Codex, or project runtime state.
Treating model output or Nucleus completion as a semantic commit.

consumers.statement: The local operator may install and diagnose Semantics, maintain explicitly marked project registrations and intake, or recover its serial worker.

preconditions.statement: Project registration or move selects a canonical folder with the exact root participation marker; worker operation requires compatible Decisions lifecycle, Conversations exact-cwd, and Nucleus execution contracts.
Retirement requires a paused project with no unresolved assigned intake, and retained-state deletion is outside this operation.

inputs.statement: Inputs are an exact project ID and canonical root, explicit administrative command, selected intake event where applicable, or one version-matched deployment candidate.

outputs.statement: Outputs are a validated installed release, durable project or intake transition, one optional committed semantic revision, or structured readiness and recovery evidence.

data_semantics.statement: Registration activates at the current opaque Decisions watermark; moves preserve project identity and cursors, pause fences commits, and semantic success is the validated SQLite revision transaction rather than model completion.

identity_and_units.statement: Project ID is stable across moves, lifecycle event and decision IDs retain upstream identity, concept IDs are project-local stable identities, and cursors remain opaque transport positions.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: A new project intentionally excludes events before its activation watermark; the serial worker advances durable scan state and commits at most one validated semantic revision per invocation.
No wall-clock bound from an upstream decision to a semantic revision is promised.

access.statement: Administrative writes use the local Semantics CLI and owned user state; the worker receives read-only upstream contracts and gives Nucleus workspace none with no shell or web.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Registration and intake transitions are durable, one worker is cross-process serial, repository revisions are atomic and append-only, and identical mailbox redelivery is idempotent while conflicts fail.
Deployment quiesces the worker and database, backs up database plus sidecars, and restores or fails closed before releasing the worker lock when rollback cannot be proved.

operational_limits.statement: Each worker invocation processes at most one reconciliation and one Nucleus job, with one immutable managed tool, neutral cwd, workspace none, no shell, and no web.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Operation contract version 1 requires Decisions lifecycle contract 1, Conversations history contract 3, and Nucleus execution contract 1; immutable schema or tool meaning changes receive successor identities.

reliances.statement: Semantics consumes ordered decision lifecycle events and opaque cursors from Decisions.
Semantics reads exact persisted task working-directory metadata from Conversations for deepest-root project routing.
Semantics uses Nucleus for one restricted reconciliation attempt while retaining all semantic commit authority.
Deployment and recurring intake or reconciliation service lifecycle rely on per-user launchd supervision, but no dedicated installed Chancery contract describes launchd readiness.
